mainTopic: ברכות on natural wonders, on rain, and the difference between שהחיינו and הטוב והמטיב
overview: This amud continues the ברכות said on sights and events. First, a ברייתא teaches that one says עושה בראשית when the sun, moon, planets and constellations return to their positions from creation, and אביי explains that this happens every 28 years (ברכת החמה). The גמרא defines לפרקים in רבי יהודה's ruling about the sea as once in 30 days. It then rules that one says עושה בראשית on seeing the פרת and the דגלת at certain places, explains the names חדקל and פרת, and brings רבא's remarks about the people of מחוזא. Next, the גמרא asks how the משנה can give הטוב והמטיב for rain when רבי אבהו teaches a different rain blessing, מודים אנחנו לך, which ends רוב ההודאות / האל ההודאות. After rejecting a split between hearing and seeing rain, it answers that the blessing depends on how much rain fell, or on whether the person owns land. This leads to the key rule: a good thing that is yours alone gets שהחיינו, and a good thing shared with others gets הטוב והמטיב. Three challenges (a baby boy, an inheritance, and a new wine) are each answered by showing that someone else shares the good. Finally, רב הונא and רבי יוחנן disagree about whether someone who already owns something similar says a ברכה on new vessels.

steps.title: Blessing on the heavenly bodies at their starting point
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one who sees the sun, moon, planets and constellations in their original positions says עושה בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who sees the sun at the start of its cycle, the moon in its full strength, the planets in their paths, and the constellations in their proper order, says: Blessed... Who makes the work of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new ברכה: עושה בראשית, said on seeing the heavenly bodies back in the positions they had at creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the sky has returned to how it looked when הקב״ה first set it up. So the ברכה praises Him as the One Who made creation. The ברייתא does not yet say when this happens, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The sun at the start of its cycle
Who makes the work of creation (the ending of the ברכה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the famous ברכת החמה, which is still said today once every 28 years.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who sees the sun at the start of its cycle,
the moon in its strength,
and the planets in their paths,
and the constellations in their order,
says: 'Blessed... Who makes the work of creation.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא within the larger discussion of ברכות on natural sights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing the heavenly bodies in their original positions requires the ברכה of עושה בראשית.

steps.title: When does this happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the sun is actually back at the start of its cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when does this happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: when exactly does this event take place? This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule but no time. Without knowing when, a person could not know when to say the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And when is it? (a request for a time)

phrases.english: And when does it happen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the timing of the event described in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact time when the sun returns to the start of its cycle.

steps.title: אביי: every 28 years
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers: every 28 years, when the spring equinox (תקופת ניסן) falls in the hour of שבתאי on Tuesday night going into Wednesday.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Every twenty-eight years, when the cycle comes back around and תקופת ניסן falls in the hour of שבתאי, on the night of Tuesday going into Wednesday.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the time: once every 28 years, the spring equinox falls at the same moment it did at creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sun was created on the fourth day, Wednesday. When תקופת ניסן again falls at the start of Wednesday (Tuesday night), in the hour of שבתאי, the sun is back where it began. That full return takes a 28-year cycle.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Night of the third, going into the fourth' means Tuesday night, which is already the start of Wednesday in Jewish counting. The ברכה is actually said on Wednesday morning, when the sun can be seen.
steps.whatToRemember: ברכת החמה is said once every 28 years, when תקופת ניסן returns to its creation-time position.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Every twenty-eight years,
when the cycle comes back around
and the Nisan equinox falls
in the hour of Saturn,
on the night of the third day, going into the fourth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of timing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every 28 years, when תקופת ניסן falls in the hour of שבתאי on Tuesday night going into Wednesday.

steps.title: How long is 'from time to time'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה in the משנה about seeing the sea לפרקים and asks how long a gap that means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: One who sees the sea, etc., from time to time. How long a gap?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, where רבי יהודה says one blesses on the great sea only if he sees it 'from time to time.' It asks how much time must pass.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לפרקים is vague. If the person sees the sea every day, he does not keep saying the ברכה. The גמרא wants the exact gap that makes the sight 'new' again.

keyTerms.meaning: From time to time, at intervals
Up to how much? (asking for a measure)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who sees the sea, etc., from time to time.
How long a gap?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to explain a new phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much time must pass between sightings to count as לפרקים.

steps.title: Thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא in the name of רב יצחק: the gap is thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבא said in the name of רב יצחק: Thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: if 30 days have passed since the last sighting, the person says the ברכה again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thirty days is the point where the sight feels fresh again. Seeing it sooner than that does not call for a new ברכה.
steps.whatToRemember: לפרקים means once in 30 days. Under that, no new ברכה is said.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 30-day measure is used in halacha for many ברכות on natural sights, not just the sea.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rami bar Abba said in the name of Rav Yitzchak:
Thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about לפרקים.

steps.title: Blessing on the Euphrates at the Babylonian bridge
steps.stepSummary: Another ruling of רמי בר אבא / רב יצחק: one who sees the פרת at the bridge of בבל says עושה בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רמי בר אבא said in the name of רב יצחק: One who sees the פרת at the bridge of בבל says: Blessed... Who makes the work of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from the same Amoraim: seeing the פרת at a certain spot calls for the ברכה of עושה בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרת is one of the four rivers from גן עדן, so seeing it in its original course reminds us of creation. The ruling names a specific place, the bridge of בבל, where the river still flowed as it did at creation.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: And Rami bar Abba said in the name of Rav Yitzchak:
One who sees the Euphrates at the bridge of Babylonia
says: 'Blessed... Who makes the work of creation.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching from the same Amoraim on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing the פרת at the bridge of בבל requires עושה בראשית.

steps.title: After the Persians changed the river
steps.stepSummary: Now that the Persians diverted the פרת, the ברכה is only said from בי שבור and upstream.
steps.simpleTranslation: And nowadays, since the Persians changed its course, it is only from בי שבור and upstream.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds an update: since the Persians rerouted the river, the ברכה is now said only upstream of the place called בי שבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה depends on the river flowing in its creation-time path. Downstream of the change, the water runs in a man-made course, so no ברכה is said there. The rule of the ברכה stays the same; only the place where it applies has moved.

phrases.english: And nowadays, since the Persians changed it,
only from Bei Shavor and upstream.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows where step 6's ruling applies today.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the river was diverted, the ברכה is said only from בי שבור and upstream.

steps.title: רב יוסף gives a different starting point
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ברכה is said from איהי דקירא and upstream.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: From איהי דקירא and upstream.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף disagrees about where the untouched part of the river starts. He names a different place, איהי דקירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the Persian change matters and the ברכה is said only upstream of it. They only disagree about the geography, meaning where the original course begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Ihi Dekira, a town on the Euphrates

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
From Ihi Dekira and upstream.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different location from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה on the פרת applies from איהי דקירא upstream.

steps.title: Blessing on the Tigris at the Shabistana bridge
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא: one who sees the דגלת (Tigris) at the bridge of שביסתנא says עושה בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רמי בר אבא said: One who sees the דגלת at the bridge of שביסתנא says: Blessed... Who makes the work of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר אבא gives the same ברכה for the second great river, the Tigris, at a specific bridge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Tigris (חדקל) is also one of the rivers of גן עדן. Just like the פרת, it gets עושה בראשית where it still flows in its original course.

keyTerms.meaning: Shabistana, a place on the Tigris

phrases.english: And Rami bar Abba said:
One who sees the Tigris at the bridge of Shabistana
says: 'Blessed... Who makes the work of creation.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same ברכה to a second river.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing the Tigris at the bridge of שביסתנא requires עושה בראשית.

steps.title: What does the name חדקל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the name חדקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'חדקל'?
steps.whatsHappening: Having mentioned the Tigris, the גמרא asks what its Torah name חדקל means. This sets up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side point about the river's name, not about the ברכה itself. The Torah calls the Tigris חדקל (בראשית ב), and the גמרא wants to explain that name.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah's name for the Tigris
What? / What is the meaning of

phrases.english: What is 'Chidekel'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the name of the river just mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind the name חדקל.

steps.title: Its waters are sharp and light
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי: חדקל means its waters are חדין (sharp) and קלין (light).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Because its waters are sharp and light.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that חדקל is a combined word: חד (sharp) + קל (light), describing the river's water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name is split into two parts, and each part describes the water. Sharp and light water was considered good for drinking.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Because its waters are sharp and light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about חדקל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חדקל = חד + קל: its waters are sharp and light.

steps.title: What does the name פרת mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the name פרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'פרת'?
steps.whatsHappening: In the same way, the גמרא now asks what the name פרת means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the question about חדקל, now asked about the second river.

phrases.english: What is 'Perat'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question, now about the other river.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind the name פרת.

steps.title: Its waters are fruitful and multiply
steps.stepSummary: פרת means its waters פרין ורבין: they are fruitful and multiply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because its waters are fruitful and multiply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that פרת comes from פרה, 'fruitful,' because its waters are full of life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waters 'multiply' in the sense that the river is full of fish and makes the land around it fertile. Like the חדקל explanation, the name describes what the water is like.
steps.whatToRemember: Both river names describe their water: חדקל = sharp and light; פרת = fruitful and multiplying.

phrases.english: Because its waters are fruitful and multiply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about פרת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרת = its waters are fruitful and multiply.

steps.title: רבא explains three traits of the people of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the reasons for three traits of the people of מחוזא: they are sharp, ruddy, and have darting eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The people of מחוזא are sharp because they drink the water of the דגלת. They are ruddy because they have marital relations in the daytime. Their eyes dart around because they live in dark houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its side discussion about the דגלת river. רבא explains three traits of the people of מחוזא, a city on the דגלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This links to step 11, where רב אשי said the דגלת's waters are 'sharp' (חדין). רבא adds that drinking this water makes the people sharp-minded. He then gives two more traits with everyday causes.

keyTerms.meaning: the people of מחוזא, a city on the דגלת

steps.whatToRemember: This ends the section about rivers. Next, the גמרא goes back to the משנה about blessings.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
This, that the people of Mechoza are sharp —
is because they drink the water of the Tigris.
phrases.notes: This connects back to the 'sharp' (חדין) water mentioned in step 11.

phrases.english: This, that they are ruddy —
is because they have relations in the daytime.
And this, that their eyes dart around —
is because they live in dark houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הַאי דַּחֲרִיפֵי בְּנֵי מָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the דגלת and builds on the 'sharp' waters from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sharpness of the people of מחוזא comes from the דגלת's water. Their ruddiness comes from daytime relations, and their darting eyes come from living in dark houses.

steps.title: Is the blessing over rain really הטוב והמטיב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and challenges it with a teaching about when one blesses over rain. That teaching implies a different blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Over rain...' But does a person really say הטוב והמטיב over rain? Didn't רבי אבהו say (and some say a ברייתא taught): From when does one bless over rain? From when the 'groom goes out to meet the bride.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which says the blessing over rain is הטוב והמטיב. It challenges this by quoting a teaching about the rain blessing. That teaching will lead to a different blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching only says when the rain blessing begins. It starts once enough rain falls that the drops splash up from puddles, like a groom going out to meet his bride. The real clash becomes clear in the next steps, when the גמרא shows that this blessing is מודים / רוב ההודאות, not הטוב והמטיב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who is good and does good', the blessing the משנה gives for rain
'but didn't he say?', the opening of a challenge
'and some say', giving another version of the source
groom toward bride: raindrops falling into puddles and making them splash up

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not answered right away. Steps 16-21 (מאי מברכין and onward) still build the question by showing which blessing the teaching means. Step 22 restates the challenge, and step 23 begins answering it.

phrases.english: 'Over rain...' (quoting the Mishnah)
phrases.notes: Quotes the משנה, which says one blesses הטוב והמטיב over rain.

phrases.english: And over rain does one bless 'Who is good and does good'?
But didn't Rabbi Abbahu say,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
From when does one bless over rain —
from when the groom goes out to meet the bride.
phrases.notes: Raindrops hitting puddles so that the water below splashes up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל הַגְּשָׁמִים ״הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב״ מְבָרֵךְ? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the river discussion and returns to the משנה's ruling on rain.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one blesses הטוב והמטיב over rain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source describes a separate rain blessing with its own starting point. The next steps show its wording is a thanksgiving blessing, not הטוב והמטיב.

steps.title: What is the wording of the rain blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which blessing רבי אבהו's teaching is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What blessing does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what words make up the rain blessing mentioned in the teaching. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching said when to bless but not what to say. Finding out the wording is what sharpens the challenge against the משנה.

phrases.english: What blessing does one recite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of the blessing whose timing step 15 gave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of the rain blessing.

steps.title: רב יהודה: We thank You for every drop
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה gives the opening words: 'We thank You for each and every drop You brought down for us.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: 'We thank You for each and every drop that You brought down for us.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by giving the main words of the rain blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a thanksgiving blessing (מודים), which is clearly different from הטוב והמטיב. That difference is what creates the challenge against the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
'We thank You
for each and every drop
that You brought down for us.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing opens with 'מודים אנחנו לך for every drop You brought down for us.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ending of the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן ends the blessing with the words of נשמת, 'if our mouths were full of song as the sea', through 'תשתחוה', and closes with ברוך אתה ה׳ רוב ההודאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן ends it like this: 'If our mouths were full of song like the sea... we could not thank You enough, ה׳ our God,' continuing until 'shall bow down.' 'Blessed are You ה׳, [God of] abundant thanksgivings.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds the closing part of the blessing, taken from the prayer נשמת, and gives its final חתימה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the blessing is complete, and its חתימה is רוב ההודאות. The phrase רוב ('most' or 'abundant') is what the גמרא questions next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'if our mouths were full of song as the sea', from נִשְׁמַת
'shall bow down', the end point of the quoted passage

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan concludes it like this:
'If our mouths were full of song as the sea, etc.'
we would not be able
to thank You enough, O Lord our God,'
until 'shall bow down.'
phrases.notes: The wording of נשמת said on שבת morning.

phrases.english: 'Blessed are You, O Lord, [God of] abundant thanksgivings.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the ending to רב יהודה's opening.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing continues with נשמת and closes with רוב ההודאות.

steps.title: Why 'most' thanks and not 'all' thanks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the closing words רוב ההודאות. Doesn't all thanks belong to ה׳?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Most thanksgivings' and not 'all thanksgivings'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the closing, רוב ההודאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רוב can sound like 'most', as if only some of the thanks is due to ה׳. That would be wrong, because all thanks belongs to Him.

phrases.english: 'Most thanksgivings'
and not all thanksgivings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the closing words given in step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Most' suggests that only part of all thanks belongs to ה׳.

steps.title: רבא changes the wording to 'the God of thanksgivings'
steps.stepSummary: רבא says to change the closing to האל ההודאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Say instead, 'the God of thanksgivings.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by changing the wording of the closing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: האל ההודאות calls ה׳ the God to whom thanks belongs, with no hint of 'most'. This avoids the problem of step 19.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Say: 'the God of thanksgivings.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The closing reads רוב ההודאות, which sounds like 'most'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The closing should read האל ההודאות.

steps.title: רב פפא: Say both phrases
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא concludes that we say both רוב ההודאות and האל ההודאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, let us say both of them: 'abundant thanksgivings' and 'the God of thanksgivings.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the wording by combining both versions in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there are two ways to word the closing, רב פפא says both to cover each view. Joining versions like this is a well-known approach of רב פפא (he says הלכך נימרינהו לתרוייהו in other places too).

keyTerms.meaning: let us say both of them

steps.whatToRemember: The rain blessing is a thanksgiving blessing: מודים... ending האל ההודאות / רוב ההודאות. This is why the משנה's הטוב והמטיב seems to clash with it. The next step brings back the challenge from step 15, and steps 23-28 answer it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Therefore, let us say both of them,
'abundant thanksgivings' and 'the God of thanksgivings.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִלְכָּךְ נֵימְרִינְהוּ לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings together the original wording (step 18) and רבא's change (step 20).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rain blessing closes with both רוב ההודאות and האל ההודאות.

steps.title: The contradiction about the rain blessing returns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the two rain blessings still contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that a problem is still open. The משנה says the blessing on rain is הטוב והמטיב, but we just learned a different blessing, מודים אנחנו לך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17-21 built a full blessing for rain that starts with מודים and ends with רוב ההודאות / האל ההודאות. The משנה, however, gives the short blessing הטוב והמטיב for rain. So which one is correct? The steps that follow will try to make room for both.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is still difficult (an unresolved contradiction)
'Who is good and does good', a blessing on shared good news or gain
'We thank You', the rain blessing taught earlier

phrases.english: But it is still difficult!
phrases.notes: The contradiction between the משנה (הטוב והמטיב) and the מודים blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the wording of the מודים blessing (steps 16-21), the גמרא returns to the challenge it opened in step 15: the משנה's הטוב והמטיב against רבי אבהו's blessing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two different blessings given for rain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rain cannot have two different required blessings unless they apply to different situations.

steps.title: Hearing about rain versus seeing rain
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the משנה's הטוב והמטיב is for someone who heard about the rain, and מודים is for someone who saw it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is where he heard about the rain. That case is where he saw it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by splitting the cases. If you only hear that rain fell, you say הטוב והמטיב. If you actually see it falling, you say מודים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a classic 'two different cases' answer. Each blessing gets its own situation, so the sources no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)

phrases.english: It is not difficult,
this is where he heard (that rain fell),
that is where he actually saw it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two blessings seem to conflict for the same event.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each blessing applies to a different way of experiencing the rain.

steps.title: Hearing about rain is just good news
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first answer: hearing about rain is simply good news, which the משנה already lists separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he heard about it, that is the same as good news. And we learned in the משנה: on good news one says 'Blessed is He Who is good and does good'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the hearing/seeing answer. The משנה already has a separate rule for good news, so there would be no reason to list rain on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists rain and good news as two separate items. If 'rain' meant only hearing about rain, it would just be one more example of good news, and the separate listing would be pointless. So the משנה's rain case must be about seeing the rain.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the hearer makes no blessing. He does say הטוב והמטיב. The problem is only that the משנה would then have no reason to mention rain separately.

phrases.english: Where he heard, that is the same as good tidings,
and we learned: on good tidings
one says 'Blessed is He Who is good and does good'!
phrases.notes: So the משנה's separate mention of rain would be extra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 23.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would make the משנה's separate rain clause redundant with its good-news clause.

steps.title: A little rain versus a lot of rain
steps.stepSummary: New answer: both cases involve seeing the rain. מודים is for a little rain, and הטוב והמטיב is for a lot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both cases are where he saw it, and there is no difficulty. This is where a little rain came, and that is where a lot came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the hearing/seeing idea and offers a new split. Both blessings are for seeing rain. The difference is how much rain fell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both cases now involve seeing, the משנה's rain clause is no longer redundant. A little rain gets the thanksgiving blessing מודים, and a heavy, abundant rain gets הטוב והמטיב.

phrases.english: Rather: both this and that are where he saw it,
and it is not difficult:
this is where a little came,
that is where a lot came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by amount of rain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the difference was hearing versus seeing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both involve seeing. The blessing depends on how much rain fell.

steps.title: Owning land versus not owning land
steps.stepSummary: Alternative answer: both cases are a lot of rain. Someone who owns land says הטוב והמטיב, and someone who does not says מודים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: both are where a lot of rain came, and it is not difficult. This is where he owns land, and that is where he does not own land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second possible answer. The split is not about the amount of rain but about whether the person owns land that the rain helps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A landowner gets a personal benefit from the rain, so he says הטוב והמטיב as in the משנה. Someone without land only gives general thanks with מודים. This answer is set up for the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
both this and that are where a lot came,
and it is not difficult —
this is where he has land,
that is where he has no land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא דַּאֲתָא טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second resolution alongside the little/a lot answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by land ownership
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the difference was the amount of rain.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with heavy rain, the blessing depends on whether the person owns land.

steps.title: A private gain gets שהחיינו, not הטוב והמטיב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the land answer: a gain that belongs only to you gets שהחיינו, and הטוב והמטיב is said only when others share in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does someone who owns land say 'Who is good and does good'?! But we learned: if one built a new house or bought new vessels, he says 'Blessed... Who has kept us alive and brought us to this time.' Only if it is his and others' does he say 'Who is good and does good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the land-owner answer using a משנה about new things. A benefit that is yours alone gets שהחיינו. הטוב והמטיב is only for a benefit shared with others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By that rule, a man whose own private land gets rain is like someone who built his own new house, so he should say שהחיינו and not הטוב והמטיב. The step 26 answer therefore seems to give the landowner the wrong blessing. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (introduces a source used to challenge)
The blessing 'Who has kept us alive', for a new personal joy

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two blessings. שהחיינו is for a good thing that is yours alone. הטוב והמטיב is for a good thing that also benefits others.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic halachic rule that separates שהחיינו (private benefit) from הטוב והמטיב (shared benefit), and the rest of the sugya builds on it.

phrases.english: One who has land recites 'Who is good and does good'?!
But we learned: if one built a new house,
or bought new vessels, he says:
'Blessed... Who has kept us alive and brought us to this time.'
phrases.notes: This is for something that belongs to him alone.

phrases.english: If it is his and others' —
he says 'Who is good and does good'?
phrases.notes: So הטוב והמטיב requires a shared benefit, not private ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִית לֵיהּ אַרְעָא הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב מְבָרֵךְ? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the land-ownership answer of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a landowner says הטוב והמטיב on rain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A private benefit gets שהחיינו. Only a shared benefit gets הטוב והמטיב. So a private landowner should say שהחיינו.

steps.title: Partnership gets one blessing, sole ownership gets the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there is no contradiction. The משנה's הטוב והמטיב is for land owned with a partner, and שהחיינו is for land owned alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this case is where he has a partnership, and that case is where he has no partnership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 27 by splitting the land owner into two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said that a gain belonging only to you gets שהחיינו, so a land owner should not say הטוב והמטיב. The answer is that the משנה is about someone who owns land together with a partner. Because the rain helps the partner too, he says הטוב והמטיב. Someone who owns land alone says שהחיינו.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not really contradict
Partnership; shared ownership with someone else
This one… that one…; used to split two sources into two different cases

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where he has a partnership,
that is where he has no partnership.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ שׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case (אוקימתא): partner versus sole owner
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any land owner says הטוב והמטיב, which clashes with the rule that a private gain gets שהחיינו
steps.terutzMaskana: Partner says הטוב והמטיב; sole owner says שהחיינו

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the partnership rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states the rule outright: for what is yours alone, say שהחיינו; for what is yours and your friend's, say הטוב והמטיב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it was taught in a ברייתא: The short version of the matter is this. For what is his own, he says 'Blessed… Who has kept us alive and sustained us.' For what is his and also his friend's, he says 'Blessed… Who is good and does good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the general rule in its simplest form. A good thing that belongs only to you gets שהחיינו. A good thing shared with others gets הטוב והמטיב. This backs up the partnership answer in step 28.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא; here it brings support, not a challenge
The short version of the matter; the general rule
Who has kept us alive and sustained us; the blessing for a private joy
Who is good and does good; the blessing for a shared joy

steps.whatToRemember: The basic rule is that good for you alone gets שהחיינו, and good shared with others gets הטוב והמטיב.
steps.confusionAlert: The same word וְהָתַנְיָא can introduce support, as it does here, or a challenge, as it does in the very next step. Look at what the source is being used for.

phrases.english: And so it was taught:
The short version of the matter is,
for what is his own, he says:
'Blessed… Who has kept us alive and sustained us,'
for what is his and his friend's,
he says: 'Blessed… Who is good and does good.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 28
steps.raayaObject: The partnership versus sole ownership split
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating the general rule for שהחיינו and הטוב והמטיב

steps.title: Challenge from the birth of a baby boy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether one never says הטוב והמטיב when alone. A ברייתא says a man told his wife had a boy says הטוב והמטיב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it true that wherever no one else is with him, he does not say 'Who is good and does good'? But it was taught in a ברייתא: If they told him his wife gave birth to a boy, he says 'Blessed… Who is good and does good'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule by showing a case where the good news seems to be the father's alone, yet he says הטוב והמטיב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הטוב והמטיב needs someone else to share the good, why does a new father say it? The good news seems to be his own personal joy.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife gave birth to a boy

phrases.english: And is it true that wherever
there is no other person with him
he does not say 'Who is good and does good'?
But it was taught:
If they told him his wife gave birth to a boy,
he says 'Blessed… Who is good and does good'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּלֵית לְאַחֲרִינָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ לָא מְבָרֵךְ הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule established in steps 28-29
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that הטוב והמטיב is said only when others share the good
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא has a father say הטוב והמטיב over what seems to be his own private joy

steps.title: The wife shares the joy
steps.stepSummary: In the case of the baby boy, the wife also shares the good, because she is happy to have a boy too.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, his wife is with him, since she is also happy about a boy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the father is not alone in this good news.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother is happy about the baby boy too. So the joy is shared, and הטוב והמטיב fits the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: There too; the same rule applies in that case
It pleases her; she is happy

phrases.english: There too,
his wife is with him,
since she is happy about a boy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a partner in the good is present
steps.terutzMaskana: The wife shares the joy, so the rule holds

steps.title: Challenge from an inheritance
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when a father dies and the son inherits him, the son first says דיין האמת and later says הטוב והמטיב. The son seems to benefit alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If his father died and he inherits him, at first he says 'Blessed… the true Judge,' and in the end he says 'Blessed… Who is good and does good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge: an heir who seems to gain alone, yet says הטוב והמטיב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son says דיין האמת over the sad news of the death. Later, when he receives the inheritance, he says הטוב והמטיב. If the inheritance is only his, he should have said שהחיינו.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source as a challenge or proof
The true Judge; the blessing said over bad news

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If his father died and he inherits him,
at first he says:
'Blessed… the true Judge,'
and in the end he says:
'Blessed… Who is good and does good.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מֵת אָבִיו וְהוּא יוֹרְשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the same rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that הטוב והמטיב needs others to share the good
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An heir seems to gain alone, yet he says הטוב והמטיב

steps.title: Brothers share the inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a son who has brothers inheriting together with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, he has brothers who inherit along with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the heir is not alone, because his brothers inherit with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is read as a case with several heirs. The inheritance is shared, so הטוב והמטיב is correct.

phrases.english: There too,
he has brothers
who inherit along with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 32
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to one with partners (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzMaskana: Brothers share the inheritance, so the rule holds

steps.title: Challenge from switching to a new wine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a change of wine needs no new בורא פרי הגפן. רבי יוחנן adds that one still says הטוב והמטיב, even though the wine seems to be the drinker's own pleasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A change of wine does not need a new blessing; a change of place does need a new blessing. And רבי יוסף בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even though they said a change of wine does not need a new blessing, he does say 'Blessed… Who is good and does good'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge: a person drinking a new wine says הטוב והמטיב, which seems to be a private pleasure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving to a new place requires a new blessing on the wine, but switching to a new wine does not. Even so, רבי יוחנן says that a new wine gets הטוב והמטיב. The question is how this fits a rule that requires someone to share the good.

keyTerms.meaning: A change of wine; switching to another wine
A change of place; moving somewhere else
The great אמורא of ארץ ישראל, quoted here by רבי יוסף בר אבא

phrases.english: Come and hear:
a change of wine does not need a new blessing,
a change of place does need a new blessing.
And Rabbi Yosef bar Abba said
in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Even though they said
a change of wine does not need a new blessing,
he does say: 'Blessed… Who is good and does good'!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שִׁינּוּי יַיִן אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge against the same rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that הטוב והמטיב needs others to share the good
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A new wine seems to be one person's own pleasure, yet רבי יוחנן says he says הטוב והמטיב
steps.confusionAlert: The 'blessing' that a change of wine does not need is בורא פרי הגפן. The הטוב והמטיב is a separate blessing of thanks for the better or additional wine.

steps.title: Friends at the meal share the new wine
steps.stepSummary: The new-wine case is about a group meal, where others are drinking with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, there are members of the group drinking with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge: the drinker is not alone, because his group shares the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's ruling is about a group meal where everyone enjoys the new wine. Since the good is shared, הטוב והמטיב fits. All three challenges are answered the same way, so the rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Members of the group; people eating the meal together

steps.whatToRemember: הטוב והמטיב is said only when others share the good: a partner, a wife, brothers, or friends at the meal. When the good is yours alone, you say שהחיינו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sugya is the source for the halacha that a new wine at a meal gets הטוב והמטיב only when others are drinking it too.

phrases.english: There too,
there are members of the group
who are drinking with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 34 and closes the series of challenges
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that others share the good
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He drinks the new wine alone
steps.terutzMaskana: Friends at the meal drink with him, so the rule holds

steps.title: Returning to the case of a new house or vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה to set up a discussion of what counts as new.
steps.simpleTranslation: One built a new house or bought new vessels, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the משנה’s case. This sets up the next question: does it matter if the owner already has something similar?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted line names two new acquisitions. The rulings that follow discuss when their blessing is required.

phrases.english: One built a new house
and bought new vessels, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּנָה בַּיִת חָדָשׁ וְקָנָה כֵּלִים חֲדָשִׁים וְכוּ׳.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the shared-benefit discussion to the משנה’s case of a new acquisition.

steps.title: A similar possession removes the need to bless
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the משנה’s blessing to someone who does not already own something similar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: They taught this only when he has nothing similar. But if he has something similar, he does not need to bless.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא narrows when the blessing applies. Already owning something similar means no blessing is needed for this acquisition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the item being newly acquired is not enough by itself. He also looks at whether the person already has one like it.

keyTerms.meaning: he does not need to bless

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין לוֹ כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: They taught this only when he has nothing similar to them,
but if he has something similar to them—
he does not need to bless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the blessing in the quoted משנה to a case where the owner lacks something similar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב הונא, someone who already owns something similar does not need to bless on this acquisition.

steps.title: A similar possession does not remove the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: even someone who owns something similar must bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even if he has something similar to them, he must bless.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite ruling for someone who already owns something similar. He says that person still needs to bless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is about the effect of an existing similar possession. רב הונא says it removes the need to bless; רבי יוחנן says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who disagrees with רב הונא

steps.whatToRemember: For רב הונא, already owning something similar matters. For רבי יוחנן, the new acquisition still requires a blessing.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even if he has something similar to them,
he must bless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא about the very case he excluded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, owning something similar does not remove the need to bless.
